name: Una Vida
life: Una learned to read at the same table where she now tutors. She deliberately leaves the teacher's chair empty on Thursday evenings so a student with another kind of knowledge can use it first. Monday often includes a stop at the foot of Harbor Viaduct, where Una pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: One of my students can read the tiny block letters upside down. He learned setting type. I asked him to teach Thursday's class and chose a seat at the back.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a boxy denim jacket and a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair. Una has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with short black hair swept back. Una steadies a cup with both hands while listening during a conversation.
personality: Una enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Una is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To give the former typesetter an evening at the front of the class.
family: Dina Hooper is Una’s half-sibling. Una picks the meeting place. Dina sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The missing name on the stern*, Dina says, “I kept the original stencil on the back of a cupboard door.”
connections: Cal Esmond. A reading class and a thesis both depend on letting a former typesetter correct the map.

reactions.situation: A collector offers cash for the unexamined atlas
reactions.response: Una asks the bookseller to put the atlas somewhere safe while its ownership is checked.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Una asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.

reactions.situation: If a family plan changes at the door
reactions.response: Una keeps a place for the late person without making the others postpone their meal.
